schema_ddl:
CREATE TABLE PRODUCT (
    PRODUCT_ID INT,
    PRODUCT_NAME VARCHAR(255),
    UNIT_PRICE INT,
    PRIMARY KEY (PRODUCT_ID),
    CHECK (UNIT_PRICE > 0)
);

CREATE TABLE SALES (
    PRODUCT_ID INT,
    SELLER_ID INT,
    BUYER_ID INT,
    SALE_DATE DATE,
    QUANTITY INT,
    PRICE INT,
    FOREIGN KEY (PRODUCT_ID) REFERENCES PRODUCT(PRODUCT_ID),
    CHECK (QUANTITY > 0),
    CHECK (PRICE > 0)
);
q1: SELECT P.PRODUCT_ID, P.PRODUCT_NAME FROM PRODUCT P INNER JOIN ( SELECT PRODUCT_ID FROM SALES GROUP BY PRODUCT_ID HAVING MIN(SALE_DATE) >= '2019-01-01' AND MAX(SALE_DATE) <= '2019-03-31' ) S ON (P.PRODUCT_ID = S.PRODUCT_ID)
q2: SELECT DISTINCT PRODUCT_ID, PRODUCT_NAME FROM PRODUCT P RIGHT JOIN SALES S USING(PRODUCT_ID) WHERE SALE_DATE>='2019-01-01' AND SALE_DATE<'2019-04-01' AND PRODUCT_ID NOT IN (SELECT PRODUCT_ID FROM SALES WHERE SALE_DATE<'2019-01-01' OR SALE_DATE>='2019-04-01' )
q1_prompt_sql: SELECT P.PRODUCT_ID, P.PRODUCT_NAME FROM PRODUCT P INNER JOIN ( SELECT PRODUCT_ID FROM SALES GROUP BY PRODUCT_ID HAVING MIN(SALE_DATE) >= '2019-01-01' AND MAX(SALE_DATE) <= '2019-03-31' ) S ON (P.PRODUCT_ID = S.PRODUCT_ID)
q2_prompt_sql: SELECT DISTINCT PRODUCT_ID, PRODUCT_NAME FROM PRODUCT P RIGHT JOIN SALES S USING(PRODUCT_ID) WHERE SALE_DATE>='2019-01-01' AND SALE_DATE<'2019-04-01' AND PRODUCT_ID NOT IN (SELECT PRODUCT_ID FROM SALES WHERE SALE_DATE<'2019-01-01' OR SALE_DATE>='2019-04-01' )
explanation: Q1 and Q2 are not semantically equivalent. Q1 selects products whose all sales occurred within the date range '2019-01-01' to '2019-03-31'. Q2 selects products that have at least one sale in that range and no sale outside that range. These are different conditions, leading to different results in some cases.
counterexample_dsp: A product with sales on '2019-01-15' and '2019-04-01' will be excluded by Q1 (because max(SALE_DATE) exceeds '2019-03-31') but included by Q2 (because the subquery excludes the product only if it has any sale outside the range).
